_meta.description: Suburban-SOC unified security index. Pins ECS fields to keyword/ip/date so cross-index aggregations and dashboards are consistent (fixes the dynamic text+keyword drift that silently failed shard aggregations). WS0.3: tenant.id is a first-class keyword. WS0.5: backed by a per-tenant data stream (logstash-security-<tenant>) under ILM policy logstash-security-ilm. #249/#250: command-line/script-block-shaped fields (process.args, *CommandLine, *ScriptBlockText, *uri — explicit properties plus the long_command_fields dynamic_template) use a lowercase normalizer (so Sigma's lowercase literals match mixed-case real telemetry via wildcard-query normalization) and a raised ignore_above so long values, e.g. encoded PowerShell, aren't silently dropped from the index. #263: process.args/process.parent.args/winlog.event_data.ScriptBlockText/winlog.event_data.ImagePath (and the long_command_fields dynamic_template backing any future field of the same shape) are raised further to ignore_above:32766 — 8191 (#249/#250's original raise from the default 1024) was still below real PowerShell 4104 chunk sizes (~20000 chars) and encoded-command-line lengths, letting both PowerShell Sigma rules and system_win_suspicious_service_binpath_lolbin.yml be silently bypassed by payload length. Note ignore_above:32766 is a CHARACTER ceiling, not the Lucene per-term 32766-BYTE hard limit it's numerically equal to — multi-byte UTF-8 content can exceed the byte limit while under the char ceiling, which would otherwise reject the whole document rather than just dropping the field (confirmed live during #263's review); configs/logstash.conf's ruby filter clamps byte-oversized values before they reach Elasticsearch to prevent that, tagging pipeline.byte_clamped separately from pipeline.truncated. Aggregations/sorts on these fields return the lowercased form; _source keeps original casing for Discover/evidence (except the rare byte-clamped case, where _source itself is clamped too — no way to preserve full fidelity there without risking the same document-rejection failure).
